transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-10-28 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Marco Ruiz (Redwood); Samir Patel, Emily Zhang, Liam Ross, Ana Torres, Rajev Menon (Orbit)\n\nSummary (auto): quick status on private VPC pilot, discuss routing/NAT issues observed last week, plan for runtime upgrade to 2.1, agreement on soak tests and security docs to share.\n\nTopics:
- Networking / VPC peering and NAT behavior
- Routing & load balancing (NLB vs ALB)
- Runtime upgrade v2.1 (kernel changes, quantization support)
- Performance numbers & tuning (batching, KV cache)
- Security/KMS and audit items
- Next steps / action items\n\nTranscript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight today, 45 minutes, quick status. Samir, do you want to kick us off with what you saw last week?
[00:12] Samir Patel: yeah thanks, Jordan. we ran the overnight soak and noticed intermittent spikes on the control plane egress, so some requests hit a NAT timeout and then retried. it seemed correlated with burst from the canary batcher. p50 is fine, around 120ms, but p95 jumped to ~420-480ms during the spikes.
[00:32] Priya Nair: okay, thanks. is that from the private subnets hitting the floating NAT gateway? Rajev, can you confirm which nat gateway type you have?
[00:42] Rajev Menon: right now it's a single NAT gateway per AZ, not highly available, and we've been using a route that funnels control plane -> internet -> redwood public endpoint, because the PrivateLink hadn't been configured yet.
[00:55] Marco Ruiz: that matches what we saw in the traces - control plane retries caused session churn on the KV cache and occasional cold starts for worker pods. if control plane calls timeout they re-create ephemeral sessions, which is the source of the increased p95.
[01:12] Emily Zhang: is there a recommended pattern? we don't want to open more broadly to the internet.
[01:18] Priya Nair: recommended is PrivateLink or VPC peering with routes for the control plane; alternatively configure a highly available NAT (or NAT Gateway per AZ) if PrivateLink isn't possible. PrivateLink gives lower variance. we can share a manifest.
[01:32] Samir Patel: we'll prefer PrivateLink, but we need security team's signoff. Liam, any blockers for PrivateLink/SLA on your side?
[01:40] Liam Ross: main concerns: TLS mutual auth, audit logs hitting our SIEM, and we want KMS integration so keys never leave our vault. if PrivateLink supports mTLS and we can push logs to our collector, it's acceptable. also need SOC2 scope docs.
[01:54] Jordan Lee: that's understood. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit log forwarding; Priya will share the security pack.
[02:02] Priya Nair: yes, I have the integration guide, and we'll include the step-by-step for KMS and audit log config. note: the current pilot is on our v2.0 runtime; v2.1 has a kernel change that reduces KV cache miss penalty and improves tail latency, so the upgrade should help p95.
[02:20] Ana Torres: curious - what's in v2.1 exactly? is it quantization changes too?
[02:25] Marco Ruiz: short version: improved attention kernel selection, better continuous batching heuristics, and a fix for KV cache eviction that reduced cold path restarts. quantization support is improved for 4-bit paths but it's an opt-in change; we'll provide recommended config for your workload.
[02:42] Samir Patel: can we run a canary first? we have about 50k tokens/day in the pilot, so we can shift 10% traffic to v2.1 and watch.
[02:49] Priya Nair: absolutely. we usually recommend a canary of 5-10% for 24-48h then 25% then full. we'll provide helm manifest changes to set image tag and runtime flags.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: regarding the NAT timeouts - we saw retries at the control plane caused by ephemeral host ports running out. one easy fix is increasing the ephemeral port range and adding a dedicated NAT per AZ. Rajev, can you confirm if you can provision that this week?
[03:12] Rajev Menon: should be able to, but provisioning windows require change freeze exceptions. I'll coordinate with infra schedule and try for 10/30.
[03:20] Emily Zhang: also wanted to raise costs - our finance lead flagged the dedicated NAT and larger instances. any guidance on cost mitigation while keeping tail latency low?
[03:29] Marco Ruiz: two levers: batching and KV cache. increasing batch size from 4->8 improved throughput but increases median slightly; however it reduced p95 when the cache hit rate improved. Also quantization for embeddings reduces GPU memory and costs. we'll run a targeted perf test for batching=8, seq=1024 and share results.
[03:48] Ana Torres: results from last week's run - we attached a CSV in the shared folder but in summary: batching=4 p50 110ms p95 430ms, batching=8 p50 130ms p95 300ms (when KV hit rate >90%).
[04:02] Priya Nair: thanks, that's helpful. Marco and I will tweak the batching heuristics and send tuned config. you might see a 10-20% cost improvement depending on traffic shape.
[04:12] Liam Ross: on security docs: please include the exact ciphers we use for TLS, the mTLS instructions, and the retention policy for audit logs. we also need SSO/SAML guidance for RBAC.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: we'll include all that. Priya will put together the security pack and an annotated checklist for your compliance team.
[04:30] Samir Patel: one operational item - during the spike we saw one worker pod restarted and lost KV cache, which triggered a higher latency cohort. is there a graceful restart pattern?
[04:40] Marco Ruiz: yes, we can enable pre-warm and graceful drain hooks so worker pods dump KV to local persistent cache before termination; alternatively set minReadySeconds to allow traffic to drain. we'll share recommended Kubernetes snippets.
[04:53] Ana Torres: perfect. also, we noticed some transcription issues in logs - the telemetry labels came back with 'redler' instead of 'redwood' in some traces; small but might confuse our dashboards.
[05:03] Priya Nair: that's from an older agent version; v2.1 fixes some of the telemetry naming collisions. we'll call out the agent version in the manifest.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: quick recap - action items: Priya provides v2.1 manifest + security pack, Marco runs perf with batching=8, Samir shares last 72h logs, Rajev attempts HA NAT by 10/30, Liam to compile compliance list. schedule: run a 24-48h canary starting after manifest is applied.
[05:30] Emily Zhang: timeline sounds good. one ask - can you include a quick cost estimate for running dedicated NAT per AZ vs PrivateLink cost delta? our finance wants a ballpark.
[05:40] Marco Ruiz: yes we can run a delta estimate and include ranges; won't be exact but should be enough for decisioning.
[05:47] Jordan Lee: ok great. any final questions?
[05:51] Samir Patel: none from me. thanks everyone.
[05:53] Liam Ross: no, thanks.
[05:55] Jordan Lee: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Link references: Pilot perf CSV (internal): https://redwood.app/pilot/orbit/perf-2026-10-27.csv ; Upgrade manifest draft: https://redwood.app/pilot/orbit/manifest-v2.1-draft.yaml ; Security pack (short): https://redwood.app/pilot/orbit/security-pack-2026-10-28.pdf\n\nClosing recap (auto):\n- Provide v2.1 runtime manifest and upgrade checklist (Priya) by 2026-10-30.\n- Customer to run 24-48h canary and soak test, share logs (Samir, Rajev) by 2026-11-03.\n- Redwood to run targeted perf test (Marco) and cost delta estimate (Marco) by 2026-10-31.\n- Security deep dive scheduled after review of security pack (TBD week of 2026-11-02).\n\nEnd of transcript.
